7
A goods train passes through a station at a steady speed of 10 m s–1 at time t = 0. An express
train is at rest at the station. The express train leaves the station with a uniform acceleration of
0.5 m s–2 just as the goods train goes past. Both trains move in the same direction on straight,
parallel tracks.
At which time t does the express train overtake the goods train?
A
6 s
B
10 s
C
20 s
D
40 s

hints: Notice overtaking means both trains have the same displacement $s$ from the station at the same time $t$.
Write $s = vt$ for the $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ goods train and $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ and $a = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for the express train.
Set $10t$ equal to $\frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times t^2$ and solve for the non-zero $t$, cancelling one factor of $t$.
walkthrough: Overtake means same starting point and same displacement at time $t$. Both start at the station at $t = 0$.
For the goods train at steady speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $s_g = vt = 10t$.
For the express train with $u = 0$ and $a = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$: $s_e = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 = 0 + 0.5 \times 0.5 \times t^2 = 0.25t^2$.
Set displacements equal: $0.25t^2 = 10t$. Divide by $t$ for $t > 0$: $0.25t = 10$.
Solve: $t = 10 / 0.25 = 40\text{ s}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too short for the accelerating train to cover the $10t$ distance of the goods train starting from rest.

B.explanation: At $10\text{ s}$ the express speed is only $at = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, still slower than the $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ goods train, so it cannot have caught up.

C.explanation: At $20\text{ s}$ the express just reaches $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, equal to the goods train speed, so its average speed is lower and its displacement is still only half.

D.explanation: Displacements are equal when $10t = 0.25t^2$, giving $t = 40\text{ s}$.
